title: Database overview
text: new database launched around 2022, another ICES stomach data base. relaunching data, format also changed. single StomachDataFullOutput.csv 4 .csv file version (one data type) current format. data still reuploaded new format. section serves guide identify data need reuploaded new format. compare data coverage live version new database, last online version old database. old export 131MB, big bundle. Instead, data-raw/build_old_db_summary.R aggregates year/country/ecoregion predator-count summary (inst/extdata/old_database_summary.csv) ships package. old export uses full country names rather ISO codes new database uses, mapped hand building summary. also ecoregion column, classified regions Latitude/Longitude: east 13°E Baltic Sea; east 9°E also Baltic Sea south 56°N (picks Danish straits/Kattegat); everything else Greater North Sea. Note merges Celtic Seas Greater North Sea (Celtic Seas doesn’t much old data isn’t easy split coordinates alone). Importantly, section compares counts. matched IDs! may therefore given column say positive, fish uploaded. necessarily mean fish re-uploaded . tried match individual predator records ID falling back comparing counts, doesn’t work almost entire database. means nearly every country, way check whether specific old predator record made new database. Specifically, tried, order: SampleNo (old) FishID (new) – documented (related FishStomachs package’s format notes) “unique country, year, quarter, ship” rather globally unique, joined composite key country + year + ship + fish_id. find real matches (predator AphiaID agreed 100% ~36,700 matched rows, way consistent coincidence), key wasn’t unique: matched rows old rows going , meaning keys matched one predator. Progressively tightened key month, day, Haul/haul_no Station/station_number. full key country + year + month + day + ship + haul_no + station_number + fish_id finally gives clean match: 1,453 rows, zero keys matching one predator, 100% predator AphiaID agreement. , 1,453 matches Latvia.. checked Denmark specifically, dropping way back just year + month + ship + haul_no + station_number (day, fish_id), still zero overlapping haul-events, despite ship codes clearly shared two exports (e.g. "26D4" appears Danish ship code ). Hence, following plots compares counts unique predators, individual records. diff n_new - n_old, .e. difference many predators exist given year/country/region. positive bar means new database predators old export year/country; negative means fewer. Note old export covers 2014. Positive bars 2015 onwards just mean new database since collected data old database never .
code: country_map <- c(   "Belgium" = "BE", "Germany" = "DE", "Denmark" = "DK", "France" = "FR",   "United Kingdom" = "GB", "Ireland" = "IE", "Latvia" = "LV",   "The Netherlands" = "NL", "Norway" = "NO", "Poland" = "PL", "Sweden" = "SE" ) country_name_map <- setNames(names(country_map), country_map)  n_old <- readr::read_csv(   system.file("extdata", "old_database_summary.csv", package = "stomachr"),   show_col_types = FALSE ) n_new <- dat |>   distinct(tbl_predator_information_id, year, country, ecoregion) |>   count(ecoregion, year, country, name = "n_new")  cmp <- full_join(n_new, n_old, by = c("ecoregion", "year", "country")) |>   mutate(     across(c(n_new, n_old), \(x) coalesce(x, 0L)),     diff = n_new - n_old   ) range(n_old$year, na.rm = TRUE) #> [1] 1963 2014

title: Database overview
text: First look total difference n summed across every country, breaking country region. Bars smaller 5 predators either way dropped focus meaningful differences.
code: year_breaks <- function(n = 10) {   function(x) {     rng <- range(x, na.rm = TRUE)     if (rng[1] == rng[2]) {       return(rng[1])     }     sort(unique(round(scales::extended_breaks(n = n)(rng))))   } }  missing_before_2015 <- function(data) {   data |>     filter(year < 2015) |>     summarise(n = sum(pmax(-diff, 0))) |>     pull(n) }  missing_subtitle <- function(data) {   paste0(     format(missing_before_2015(data), big.mark = ","),     " stomachs from before 2015 are missing from the new database"   ) }  diff_bar <- function(data, subtitle = NULL, facet = NULL) {   # width = 1: geom_col()'s default width is derived from the smallest gap   # between x values actually present. A country with data in only two   # widely-spaced years (e.g. 1981 and 1991) would otherwise get bars ~10   # years wide instead of ~1 -- fixing the width stops that.   p <- data |>     filter(abs(diff) >= 5) |>     ggplot(aes(year, diff, fill = diff >= 0)) +     geom_col(width = 1) +     geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +     scale_x_continuous(breaks = year_breaks(10)) +     scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#3B9AB2", `FALSE` = "#D7191C"), guide = "none") +     labs(x = "Year", y = "New database minus\nold database (predators)")   if (!is.null(facet)) p <- p + facet_wrap(facet, ncol = 3)   if (!is.null(subtitle)) p <- p + labs(subtitle = subtitle)   p }  diff_bar_country <- function(data, subtitle = NULL) {   p <- data |>     filter(abs(diff) >= 5) |>     mutate(country_name = unname(country_name_map[country])) |>     ggplot(aes(year, diff, fill = country_name)) +     geom_col(width = 1) +     geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +     scale_x_continuous(breaks = year_breaks(10)) +     scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +     labs(x = "Year", y = "New database minus\nold database (predators)", fill = "Country") +     theme(legend.position = "bottom")   if (!is.null(subtitle)) p <- p + labs(subtitle = subtitle)   p }  cmp_overall <- cmp |>   summarise(n_new = sum(n_new), n_old = sum(n_old), .by = year) |>   mutate(diff = n_new - n_old)  diff_bar(cmp_overall, subtitle = missing_subtitle(cmp_overall))

code: plot_dat <- dat |>   filter(     predator_scientific_name %in% top,     stomach_status == "food",     !is.na(prey_weight_all_ind)   ) |>   mutate(     prey_group = fct_lump_n(coalesce(prey_class, "Other"), n = 5, w = prey_weight_all_ind, other_level = "Other"),     n_pred = n_distinct(tbl_predator_information_id), .by = predator_scientific_name   ) |>   summarise(     total_weight = sum(prey_weight_all_ind),     n_pred = first(n_pred),     .by = c(predator_scientific_name, prey_group)   ) |>   mutate(frac = total_weight / sum(total_weight), .by = predator_scientific_name)  ggplot(plot_dat, aes(frac, predator_scientific_name, fill = prey_group)) +   geom_col() +   geom_text(     data = distinct(plot_dat, predator_scientific_name, n_pred),     aes(x = 1.01, y = predator_scientific_name, label = n_pred),     hjust = 0, inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3   ) +   scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Spectral") +   scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.1), expand = c(0, 0)) +   coord_cartesian(expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +   labs(x = "Diet proportion (by weight)", y = NULL, fill = "Prey class")

text: next step join four CSVs. means attaching haul file metadata predators, classifying stomach "food", "empty", "unidentified", deduplicates exact-duplicate prey rows (present national submissions), converts prey length mm cm, handles count sentinel value (9999 = unknown multiplicity), optionally imputes missing coordinates ICES rectangle midpoints (defaults "food"). Known country-specific unit issues (currently requires manual correction proceeding): predator length weight unit data (prey). want cm grams. Belgium (): pred_length mm – divide 10 Denmark (DK): ind_wgt kg – multiply 1000 Known data-quality issue, handled automatically: submissions (seen Celtic Seas data) corrupt ICESrectangle codes (e.g. "46E9" stored "46000000000", Excel read scientific notation). join_stomach_data() detects codes don’t match real ##L# format recomputes ShootLat/ShootLong. many rows affected printed function.

title: Workflow
text: Estimates missing prey weight /length via L/W parameters observed means, estimates missing predator weight length. Also creates final predator_weight column (observed weight available, otherwise estimated length). L/W parameters looked internal table (FishBase fish, Robinson 2010 invertebrates) hierarchical fallback: species -> family -> order -> class -> phylum -> universal (= 0.01, b = 3). Future versions package fit mixed models instead impute weights clever way, accounting also size, etc! : impute "prey", "pred", "" (default) method: "lw_params" (default) uses bundled L/W table; "observations" uses mean sizes records species size: impute "weight", "length", "" (default) fill_if_no_size: TRUE (default), prey recorded size borrow records species applying L/W
code: dat <- impute_size(dat, which = "both", method = "lw_params", size = "both") #> impute_size(): which = "both" | method = "lw_params" | size = "both" | #> fill_if_no_size = TRUE #>  #> Prey: 7,985 records | L/W params (unique AphiaIDs): species: 65, family: 39, #> order: 30, class: 56, phylum: 16, universal (a=0.01, b=3): 48 #> |-- both weight and length recorded: 1,767 (22.1%) #> |-- one size recorded, other estimated: 6,099 (76.4%) #> | |-- had length, estimated weight via L/W: 24 (0.3%) #> | +-- had weight, estimated length via L/W: 6,075 (76.1%) #> |-- no size recorded, imputed from other records: 115 (1.4%) #> | |-- same stomach: mean weight -> length via L/W: 8 (0.1%) #> | |-- same pred-prey pair: mean weight -> length via L/W: 104 (1.3%) #> | +-- global species mean: mean weight -> length via L/W: 3 (0.0%) #> +-- no size info in any record of that species: 4 (0.1%) (diet composition #> only, weight unusable) #>  #> Predator: 13,935 rows | L/W params (unique AphiaIDs): species: 22, family: 1 #> |-- weight and length observed: 13,935 (100.0%) #> +-- weight observed, length missing: 0 (0.0%) #>
